To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Asian crisis was characterized by regime shifts in the structural relations among currency and equity markets in the affected economies, and the regime shifts occurred in late 1987, early 1998, and late 1997.

(i) there was a structural change in the relation between the exchange rate and equity market in most Asian countries in the late 1990s, (ii) this change was associated with the Asian currency crisis, (iii) the structural change affected the volatility of equity returns more than it affected equity returns, (iv) the structural change was associated with increased correlation between equity and exchange rate returns in some Asian countries, and (v) the structural change in the exchange rate-equity market relation
the Asian crisis was characterized by regime shifts in the currency and equity markets, which were caused by information spillover, portfolio rebalancing and common information shocks.

the identification of structural breaks in the relationships between currency and equity markets in Asia during and before the recent Asian crisis.
